newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- MOBILE STAFF IN 30 MILLION STG SHAREOUT

Mobile Systems International, a small telecommunications software company started six years ago with 100,000 stg of capital, will share a 30 million stg pay-out between 100 employees after a deal with an American investor valued the business at 180 million stg. Chairman Mo Ibrahim stands to collect 15 million stg following the sale of 20 percent of the company to General Atlantic Partners for 36 million stg.
-- UB BITES BACK WITH 42 MILLION STG

United Biscuits has unveiled an 80 million stg swing into profitability, despite pressures from competitors, particularly in Australia. The removal of loss maker Keebler, its former American snacks, cookies and frozen foods operation, helped United's profit items to double. A better performance in Britain was offset by weak Continental demand and aggressive competition in Australia from Pepsico of Tazos.
-- UNITED NEWS PLEDGES TO REVIVE EXPRESS

United News and Media have pledged to turn around the ailing Express newspaper titles after unveiling its first set of interim results after its three billion stg merger with MAI, the broadcaster. The group is set to move to seven-day publishing of the Daily and Sunday Express and the launch of colour magazines to fend off their declining circulations. City analysts were surprised at the extent of the exceptional items in the results.
THE TIMES
-- BTR SPENDS 622 MILLION STG ON RESTRUCTURING AND
CUTS PAYOUT

The industrial company BTR is attempting to restore the company's fortunes by making 622 million stg of provisions and will cut its full-year dividend by 35 percent. The charges cover the costs of the company's restructuring programme, with half-year profits being wiped out by exceptional charges. BTR has said it would press on with its disposal programme.
-- FIERCE RIVALRY HITS PROFITS AT BRITISH GAS

British Gas has incurred losses of 180 million stg in its industrial and commercial gas supply business in the first half of the year as it confronted competition from rival suppliers. The company said it is making progress in renegotiating the take-or-pay contracts, which oblige it to pay above-market prices for North Sea gas. Chairman Richard Giordano said there were signs that a small number of gas suppliers were willing to renegotiate the contracts.
-- SHARES RISE TO RECORD HIGH AS INFLATION DIPS

August saw Britain's inflation rate fall back to 2.1 percent, but the underlying inflation rate, targeted by the Government, remained at 2.8 per cent for the fourth month running, in spite of City expectations. Many in the City are convinced that base rates should not fall again. Despite mild disappointment the stock market still soared to a new record on the back of positive British corporate results and a strong performance on Wall Street.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BANKS 'PLANNING NEW WAVE OF JOB CUTS'

Bifu, the banking and finance union, has warned workers in the financial services industry of job cuts as Lloyds-TSB announced the closure of 150 branches, predicting that up to 1,000 branches will eventually close, with the loss of 10,000 jobs. The financial services industry has lost 120,000 jobs in six years due to mergers and the introduction of new technology. Further consolation among building societies and insurers is expected.
-- GILLETTE TAKES OVER DURACELL IN SEVEN BILLION DOLLAR DEAL

Gillette, the consumer goods giant, has bought Duracell, the world's biggest maker of alkaline batteries in a deal worth seven billion dollars which will allow Duracell to market its products around the globe. The deal will bring a windfall for the buy-out specialist which runs a third of Duracell, Kohlberg Kravis Roberts. Gillette has been trying to branch out into other household products other than razor blades and is one of America's leading household products companies.
-- PENSIONS TRUSTEES SHUN MORGAN

The investment bank Morgan Grenfell is set to lost two billion stg of new pension business from institutional investors in the aftermath of the scandal at its unit trust division. Pension advisers have said they could not present the bank to clients as a "credible" manager until the outcome was known of an inquiry by watchdog Imro.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- MORGAN KNEW OF DEALS, SAYS YOUNG

The fund manager at the centre of the Morgen Grenfell affair, Peter Young, has said his senior managers knew about the transactions that led to the suspension of three top-performing funds, saying he went out of his way to tell them about the companies in which he bought shares. He said managers did not scrutinise his work because they trusted his previous performance. The funds he ran had been the top-performing funds before sliding through the rankings earlier this year.
-- GOKAL'S TRICKERY KEPT BCCI OVER A BARREL, COURT TOLD

Anthony Hacking QC told an Old Bailey jury how tycoon Abbas Gokal had the Bank of Credit and Commerce International "over a barrel" over the bankrolling of his business empire. He said anything Mr Gokal "touched turned into losses" and accused him of feeding BCCI false information to ensure it kept paying his debts.
-- BUSINESS WARNED OF MILLENNIUM

The government has warned of a massive global computer crash unless executives get to grips with the software implications of the millennium date change. The independent group set up to tell businesses about the problem, Taskforce 2000, has said forms had just a year-and-a-half before it would be too late. The cost to UK businesses has been estimated at 15 billion stg, with larger firms expected to spend tens of millions each.
